title: Heat Pump Rebates in Timmins 2026: Ontario's Coldest January and Cold-Climate Rules
desc: Timmins heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: January lows average -18.6C, 72% of homes predate 1981 and only cold-climate models qualify.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Timmins has the coldest January in our Ontario data (-18.6°C) and a record low of -39.3°C. A heat pump here has to be a cold-climate model, with a backup plan.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Timmins
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 7,125 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981, and 72% of the 17,890 households live in homes of that age. 78% live in an eligible type and 67% own. 8.0% report needing major repairs, the highest share in our Ontario data.
Backup is part of the plan

With a record low near -40°C, the heat pump may not carry every hour. The program allows existing wood or electric-resistance heat as backup for electric and wood homes, and new electric resistance backup for oil homes. Backup is not rebated. Ask the contractor how the controls will switch between the heat pump and the backup, and what the plan is at the coldest design temperature.

An air-source system pays $1,250 per ton up to $7,500 for electric, oil, propane and wood homes, so 6 tons reaches the cap. A gas home pays $500 per ton up to $2,000. Oil homes must remove or empty the tank with a TSSA-registered contractor.

Timmins is served by Hydro One, which does not run the rebate. Lower-income households should check the Energy Affordability Program first, which can include cold-climate heat pumps for oil-heated homes.

An oil-heated Timmins home must transition to an electric heat pump and have the tank emptied or removed by a TSSA-registered contractor, with the owner signing the tank removal attestation form. Propane homes sign it too. Leave time for the tank work, since it is part of the program conditions.

The contractor submits the pre-installation application, waits for written approval, installs, then files the post-installation application within 30 days. The cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.
claim_steps: Plan the backup heat before choosing equipment.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
